steps.note: #194: drop a PICO-8 cart on the page -> it converts, runs, and opens in the editor. $MOY_DROP is the .p8 or the .p8.png; the test runs this scenario once for each.

BASELINE for the pixel proof below: how much of tiny_dash's pink (p8 colour 14, 255,119,168) the console paints BEFORE the drop. The probe quantises the colour through RGB565 and back the way the console does -- it rasterizes 565 and page_core expands it with bit replication, so 255,119,168 reaches the canvas as 255,117,173 and an exact match on the palette value counts nothing at all (measured 2026-08-29). Counted rather than assumed, so the check does not rest on a claim about what the shell's own chrome and wallpaper use.
the same message the real drop handler posts -- real bytes, real worker
IT RUNS, part 1: the console's own assets payload names the cart that is playing

IT RUNS, part 2, and this is the one that matters: the cart's OWN _draw is painting. tiny_dash fills an 80x80 block in p8 colour 14; nothing else on this page does. A loaded-but-not-ticking cart, a shim that never called the body, or the old Python stub would all leave this at the baseline.
